r317.summary: Read #317 and the full rights doc (docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md, origin/main, 191 lines). Mapped every §-section and every discrete rule, checked all 7 inventory items against exact doc text (3 of 7 need substantive-correction flags for wording that doesn't match, 1 item's _parent asymmetry is entirely absent from the doc), located the #304 probe evidence in scripts/migrations/probes + seed-results (also absent from the doc), assessed quotability, and confirmed no existing 'R1'/'RULE-'/bracketed-tag identifier scheme to collide with (only [P]/[F]/[PE]/[LIVE] confidence tags exist).

findings.topic: 1. Doc structure — every §-section and discrete rule
findings.fact: The doc (docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md, 191 lines) has: intro block (lines 1-23: PORTED note, known-deltas bullets, Status/Scope/Supersedes, Provenance key) — §1 Three property buckets built at WRITE time [P] (26-35) — §2 Read returns EXACTLY ONE bucket [P] (37-56) — §3 Per-property sharing IS first-class [P] (59-88, includes a 2026-08-07 [LIVE] correction paragraph at 87) — §4 The database boundary IS a read boundary [F] (91-112) — §5 Changing _sharing requires _owner [P] (115-124) — §6 Rights references NOT type-constrained but entity-to-entity grants confer nothing [P] (127-135) — §7 Live-probe corroboration [PE] (137-170) split into §7.1 _viewer-alone suffices for full private-bucket read (141-148), §7.2 CREATE auto-grants caller _owner as one direct doc (149-158), §7.3 One direct rights-tier per (reference,entity) (159-170) — then two unnumbered closing sections: 'What this changes for the single-collective design' (173-179) and 'Discipline note (why this doc exists)' (182-190, contains the closing citation rule) plus attribution trailers (188, 190).
findings.evidence: git show origin/main:docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md; section headers at lines 26,37,59,91,115,127,137,141,149,159,173,182 (grep '^## |^### ' confirmed exact set, no others).

findings.topic: 1a. Inventory item — 'Three visibility gates: prop-def ∧ type ∧ instance, narrowest wins (§3, plus the widen history)'
findings.fact: SUBSTANTIVE-CORRECTION CANDIDATE (out of scope per #316). §3 does describe three AND-gates in substance — property-def _sharing, entity-type _sharing as a cap, and a 'second retention gate' keyed on the entity's OWN _sharing — but the doc never frames them as 'three gates' or says 'narrowest wins'; it literally says 'using **two** `_sharing` values' (line 61) then adds the entity-instance check as an afterthought ('Second retention gate', line 83). There is also no 'widen history' anywhere in the doc (grep for widen/narrow returned nothing outside the unrelated Provenance-key use of 'narrower confidence'). The operative sentences: line 61 '...decided per property, using **two** `_sharing` values:'; line 83 '**Second retention gate** (`aggregate.js:269-275`): ... a property is exposed at a tier only if BOTH the property-definition's `_sharing` AND the entity's own `_sharing` allow it.'
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:61,64,66-72,74-79,83; grep -in 'narrow\|widen' returned only line 22/139 (unrelated confidence-grade usage).

findings.topic: 1b. Inventory item — 'One direct rights-tier per (reference, entity)... propagation never deletes a child's own direct grant (§7.3)'
findings.fact: MATCHES, in §7.3, but the issue's two checklist bullets (this one, and 'direct/inherited separate additive layers') are two SENTENCES inside the SAME paragraph (line 163), not two separable paragraphs. Operative text — replace rule: '**The model**: a reference can hold at most one active **direct** rights-tier grant per entity. Granting a new direct tier... for a reference that already holds a direct tier on that same entity retires (soft-deletes) the old one — even via a bare, independent POST carrying no prior `_id`.' Non-extension to propagation, in the NEXT paragraph (line 165): '...this replace-on-new-direct-grant behavior is strictly **same-entity, same-reference**. It does **not** extend to parent→child propagation: granting a reference `_owner` on a parent... does **not** delete that child's own pre-existing standalone direct grant for the same reference...'
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:159-169 (§7.3).

findings.topic: 1c. Inventory item — 'Direct and inherited are separate additive layers; only the direct layer is single-tier-per-reference (§7.3)'
findings.fact: MATCHES VERBATIM — this is the last sentence of the same line-163 paragraph as 1b above, not a separate location: 'An entity's aggregated rights are the **combination of its own direct grant(s) plus whatever cascades in as inherited** from `_inheritrights` parents (§1-§2) — direct and inherited are separate, additive layers; only the direct layer is single-tier-per-reference.' Exact wording match to the issue's phrasing.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:163.

findings.topic: 1d. Inventory item — '`_sharing` and `_inheritrights` are different axes — visibility versus rights inheritance'
findings.fact: DOES NOT YET EXIST as a discrete quotable rule. grep for 'axis'/'axes' in the doc returns zero hits. The doc treats _sharing (§3, §5) and _inheritrights (§6, §7.3, and the line-10 create-time-copy note) in separate sections but never states the contrast as a rule — it is a synthesis a reader could infer, not a citable sentence anywhere in the current text.
findings.evidence: grep -in 'axis\|axes' docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md → no output; _inheritrights occurrences at lines 10,119,133,163,165,177 are all mechanism mentions, none framed as 'a different axis from _sharing'.

findings.topic: 1e. Inventory item — 'Entity CREATE auto-grants the caller _owner as one direct document aggregating as all four tiers (§7.2)'
findings.fact: MATCHES §7.2 closely, heading text is near-identical to the issue's phrasing. Heading (line 149): '### 7.2 Entity CREATE auto-grants the creating caller `_owner` — ONE direct document, aggregating as all four tiers'. Body corroborates with a dedup-by-_id probe result.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:149-158.

findings.topic: 1f. Inventory item — 'A _viewer-alone grant already suffices for full private-bucket read (§7.1)'
findings.fact: MATCHES §7.1 heading verbatim: '### 7.1 A `_viewer`-alone grant already suffices for full private-bucket read' (line 141). Core operative sentence for a citation is line 145: 'Property-tier `_sharing` (§3) does not filter on top of entity-level rights admission — entity rights decide the bucket, and the whole bucket is exposed once any grant admits the caller to it.'
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:141,145.

findings.topic: 1g. Inventory item — 'The database boundary is a read boundary (§4); changing _sharing requires _owner (§5)'
findings.fact: MATCHES both headings verbatim: §4 line 91 '## 4. The database boundary IS a read boundary  [F]'; §5 line 115 '## 5. Changing `_sharing` requires `_owner`  [P]'.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:91,115.

findings.topic: 1h. Inventory item — the _parent asymmetry (#304 probe): 'value DELETE was owner-gated while POST was editor-gated', mark with evidence and scope (probed on one property, not general)
findings.fact: ABSENT from the doc entirely — grep for '_parent' and for '304' across the whole file returns zero hits. This is a genuine gap, not a wording mismatch: nothing in the doc currently states this asymmetry in any form.
findings.evidence: grep -n '_parent' docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md → no output; grep -n '#304\|304' → no output.

findings.topic: 2. Existing citation/epistemic conventions
findings.fact: Grades used per-section as bracketed suffixes on headings: [P] (Palestrina, direct source read this pass), [F] (Finn, direct source read this pass), [PE] (Pérotin, live-probe against live Entu — 'narrower confidence than [P]/[F]', flagged at point of use), plus an inline [LIVE] tag (line 87) marking a correction added after an original claim was found stale. Provenance key defined once at line 22. Every mechanics claim in §1-§6 carries an inline `file:line` citation in backticks (e.g. `aggregate.js:86`, `middleware/auth.js:21`). §7's live-probe claims cite script + result JSON file paths instead of source file:line (lines 147, 157, 167). The closing-note rule, verbatim (line 186): '> **Claims about Entu mechanics cite `entu-api` source `file:line`, or are marked unverified. Repo docs — including findings docs — are summaries, not authority.**' Authorship trailers close the doc (lines 188, 190) using `(*MVOX:Name*)` attribution, per-contribution.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:22,87,139,147,157,167,186,188,190.

findings.topic: 3. The _parent asymmetry — #304 probe evidence location in the repo
findings.fact: Two probe scripts exist, both under scripts/migrations/probes/: probe-304-parent-append-gate-2026-09-10.ts (an earlier/adjacent probe on append-POST gating of a series _parent value, no result JSON found for it) and probe-304-parent-rights-gate-2026-09-10.ts (the definitive probe: 'THE `_parent` RIGHTS GATE, VERIFIED LIVE ON POLYPHONY' — explicitly designed to settle 'a `_parent` POST is EDITOR-gated but a `_parent` value DELETE is OWNER-gated' empirically since 'the live deployment runs NEWER code than the public source'). Its result is scripts/migrations/seed-results/probe-304-parent-rights-gate-live-2026-09-10T05-11-52-413Z.json. The ledger confirms the asymmetry live: step 'A-editor-delete-parent-value' → 403 'User not in _owner property' for an editor-only caller; step 'B2-editor-plus-expander-on-referenced' → 200 (POST succeeded once editor-on-event + expander-on-target were both present, i.e. POST is editor-gated on the entity, not owner-gated); control step 'A2-editor-delete-plain-value' → 200 (proves DELETE-is-owner-gated is specific to `_parent`, not DELETE generally); step 'A3-owner-delete-parent-value' → 200 (proves the op is possible, only rights differed). The probe's own header states the scope explicitly: tested on ONE property (`_parent`), ONE entity type (`event`), not asserted as a general DELETE-vs-POST rights rule — exactly the caveat #317 asks to preserve. As established in finding 1h, none of this is in the rights doc yet.
findings.evidence: scripts/migrations/probes/probe-304-parent-rights-gate-2026-09-10.ts:1-10 (header/QUESTION); scripts/migrations/seed-results/probe-304-parent-rights-gate-live-2026-09-10T05-11-52-413Z.json steps 'A-editor-delete-parent-value' (403), 'B2-editor-plus-expander-on-referenced' (200), 'A2-editor-delete-plain-value' (200), 'A3-owner-delete-parent-value' (200); confirmed origin/main matches working tree via `git diff origin/main -- <both files>` (empty).

findings.topic: 4. Quotable-whole test — length of each rule candidate
findings.fact: Short/OK as-is: §1 (10 lines, one paragraph+bullets), §2 (code block + 2 short paragraphs), §5 (3 bullets, ~9 lines), §7.2 heading+first paragraph (line 151, one paragraph). §7.1 and §7.2's OPERATIVE sentence (not the full subsection) is quotable whole; the surrounding probe-design narration (e.g. line 143's long single sentence describing the sequential viewer→expander→editor probe design) is not needed for the citation and is too long/narrative to quote as 'the rule'. TOO LONG as currently scoped: §3 (lines 59-88, ~30 lines spanning 3 code blocks plus a long 2026-08-07 [LIVE] correction paragraph) — cannot be quoted whole as one rule; the three sub-mechanics (prop-def sharing, type cap, entity retention gate) are each individually quotable but the section as a whole is not. §7.3 (lines 159-169) — four paragraphs (intended-not-bug ruling, the model, the distinguished-from-refuted-hypothesis caveat, practical consequence) covering at least two distinct citable rules (replace-on-same-reference; non-extension to propagation) plus a sentence-level third (additive layers, see 1c) embedded inside the first paragraph — too long to cite as one identifier, and the issue's own inventory already implicitly wants 2-3 identifiers out of it. §6 (lines 127-135, 2 paragraphs) is borderline — quotable but long for 'whole'; the two distinct rules inside it (reference not type-constrained; no group-expansion primitive / dead-reference behavior) could split into two shorter, cleaner quotes (see finding 5).
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:59-88 (§3), 127-135 (§6), 159-169 (§7.3), 141-147 (§7.1).

findings.topic: 5. Other rules in the doc beyond #317's inventory that could get identifiers (reporting only, not deciding)
findings.fact: Candidates spotted: (a) §2's tier-priority order itself — explicit grant > domain > public, first-match-wins (lines 42-51) — foundational, and is what §7.1 explicitly corroborates rather than restates. (b) §1's write-time-snapshot structural fact (line 33: 'The buckets are **snapshots taken at write time**, not computed at read time... a read returns whatever was last written') — distinct from §3's per-property mechanics, load-bearing for the §3 [LIVE] re-aggregation correction. (c) §4's 'not one JWT = one collective' nuance (line 111) — a separate citable consequence from the main boundary rule. (d) §6 splits into two separable rules: reference targets aren't type-constrained at write time (line 129) vs. a non-person grant is inert / no group-membership-expansion primitive exists (lines 131,133). (e) §7.2's practical consequence (line 155: 'what a create payload sends and what the platform actually grants the creator are different questions') — a standalone operational rule, not just corroborating narration. (f) §5's consequence bullet (line 123: auto-provisioned/invited person gets `_editor: self` not `_owner`, so cannot change own `_sharing` on their own JWT) — could stand alone from §5's main rule. (g) The closing Discipline-note citation rule itself (line 186) — a meta-rule about the DOC's own conventions rather than an Entu mechanic; #317's scope ('every rule... in the doc') is ambiguous on whether doc-conduct rules count.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md:33,42-51,111,123,129,131,133,155,186.

findings.topic: 6. Identifier scheme collisions
findings.fact: No existing 'R1'/'R2'/'RULE-' pattern or numeric bracketed rule tags anywhere in the doc. The ONLY bracketed tags present are the confidence/provenance markers [P], [F], [PE], and the one-off correction marker [LIVE] (line 87) — all defined in the Provenance key (line 22) and used as suffixes on section headings or inline correction flags, never as rule identifiers. Section numbering uses bare '§N' / '§N.M' (no letters, no dots beyond one level) for navigation only, per #317's own framing. Any new identifier scheme should avoid single/double-letter-plus-digit forms that could be visually confused with [P]/[F]/[PE], and should avoid a bare '§'-prefixed form since that's reserved for positional navigation.
findings.evidence: grep -n -E 'R[0-9]+|RULE-|\[R[0-9]|§[0-9]\.[0-9]' over docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md — only hits were §N.M navigation headings themselves (lines 141,149,159) and the pre-existing [P]/[F]/[PE]/[LIVE] provenance tags; no rule-ID pattern of any kind exists yet.

r318.summary: mvox-app.git confirmed as origin. Repo read-only checked (feature branch feat/315-... holds scripts/roadmap/render.ts dirty per the pipeline note; used git show origin/main for src/scripts, but this task's targets — deploy config, MCP infra, hooks — are all untouched by that branch). Core finding: mvox.eu today is a pure static SPA with ZERO server-side runtime — no wrangler config, no adapter-cloudflare, no +server.ts, no hooks.server.ts. Serving an MCP-over-HTTP endpoint therefore requires adding a genuinely new server component; none of the three realistic view-not-copy options (build-time bundle / runtime GitHub fetch / other repo-file-read pattern) have any existing infrastructure to build on in this repo today.

findings.topic: 1. Current deployment shape
findings.fact: mvox.eu is a pure static SPA on Cloudflare Pages with NO server-side code at all — adapter-static, fallback:index.html, no Workers Functions, no BFF routes.
findings.evidence: svelte.config.js: `import adapter from '@sveltejs/adapter-static'` with `fallback: 'index.html'`, `paths.relative: false`. `git log --follow -- svelte.config.js` shows only 2 commits ever, both adapter-static (from repo scaffold #2 onward) — adapter-cloudflare was never live on this branch's svelte.config.js. package.json devDependencies list `@sveltejs/adapter-static` only; no `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare`, no `dependencies` key at all (zero runtime npm deps). vite.config.ts comment states outright: 'This app has ssr = false and no server code at all.' `find src -iname hooks*` and `find src/routes -iname '+server.ts'` both empty. Local `build/` output (adapter-static) contains only `_app/`, `index.html`, `robots.txt` — classic static bundle, no `_worker.js`/Functions dir. No `wrangler.json`/`.toml` exists in the working tree (`find . -iname 'wrangler.json*'` empty) and `git log --all -- wrangler.json*` returns nothing — it was never committed on this branch's history.

findings.topic: 1b. architecture-decisions.md describes a superseded/aspirational BFF that is NOT what's live
findings.fact: The 'Stack' decision text (architecture-decisions.md:355-357) still says 'deployed to Cloudflare Pages + Workers via @sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare' with 'BFF pattern: SvelteKit server holds the Entu JWT in an httpOnly cookie' — but this was superseded 2026-05-23 by the CHORE-53 'Path C' decision (line 458+): browser talks to api.entu.app directly, JWT lives in localStorage, and 'hooks.server.ts becomes a no-op (no cookie session under Path C)' with `/auth/+server.ts`, `/auth/cookie/+server.ts`, `/auth/logout/+server.ts`, `/api/organizations/+server.ts` all explicitly DELETED. Team-lead-archive:157 (session-14 era) also records a since-removed `wrangler.json` with `compatibility_date`/`nodejs_compat`/`pages_build_output_dir: .svelte-kit/cloudflare` for CF-dashboard disaster recovery — none of that exists in the repo today.
findings.evidence: grep of architecture-decisions.md lines 355-647 (Path C decision + BFF elevated-ops-list sections) and josquin.md/team-lead-archive.md memory notes referencing the now-absent wrangler.json/`.svelte-kit/cloudflare` deploy path; cross-checked against the live tree which has none of it. [unverified] whether the CF Pages dashboard build-output-dir setting itself was ever updated in step with the adapter switch — could not query the CF dashboard from this read-only task; the local build artifact (adapter-static shape) is the only piece verified directly.

findings.topic: 1c. BFF today = an enumerated-but-currently-empty elevated-ops list, not a server that runs
findings.fact: The 'BFF (CF Worker)' is reserved only for OAuth coordination (client-side redirect init page, no `+server.ts`) plus a currently-empty list of future genuinely-elevated ops (transactional email, cron cleanup, federation reports). All data calls are browser-direct to `api.entu.app` because Entu's JWT `aud` claim is IP-bound and a CF Workers proxy call arrives from CF's edge IP, breaking the JWT.
findings.evidence: architecture-decisions.md:458-472, 563-587 (BFF elevated-ops list decision + rationale); `src/lib/auth/exchange.ts`, `src/lib/entu/request.ts` exist and confirm client-side direct-to-Entu calls; `src/routes/auth/[provider]/+page.svelte` is client-side only per its own doc comment.

findings.topic: 2. MCP server code / transport infra
findings.fact: No MCP code exists anywhere in the repo, and no MCP SDK dependency is installed. There is no existing HTTP-request-handling code to attach a streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint to.
findings.evidence: `grep -rli 'modelcontextprotocol\|mcp server\|streamableHttp'` across the repo (excluding node_modules/.svelte-kit) returns nothing. `grep -n '@modelcontextprotocol' package.json pnpm-lock.yaml` returns nothing. package.json has no `dependencies` field at all — only `devDependencies`.

findings.topic: 2b. nodejs_compat / process.env platform trap — currently moot, but documented for when server code returns
findings.fact: The known CF-Workers trap (`nodejs_als` doesn't expose `process`; use `nodejs_compat` or `$env/*`) is not currently live/relevant because there is no Workers runtime in this app at all right now — but it's an explicit team memory item (`project_cf_workers_process_env`) and was previously fixed live (`52a5fca` hotfix flipping `nodejs_als`→`nodejs_compat` in the now-deleted wrangler.json) before the app moved fully to adapter-static/browser-direct.
findings.evidence: josquin.md:586 ('[GOTCHA] compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_als"] does NOT expose process global ... nodejs_compat does'); team-lead-archive.md:1531-1537, 1606 (CHORE-47 migrated 5 call sites to `$env/dynamic/private`). No `nodejs_compat` string exists anywhere in the current repo (`grep -rn nodejs_compat` across *.md/*.json/*.toml returns nothing) — the flag left the repo along with wrangler.json.

findings.topic: 3. Design-question infra inventory — build-time bundle option (3a)
findings.fact: No mechanism currently stamps a git commit SHA into the build. SvelteKit's own generated `_app/version.json` exists but holds only a numeric build timestamp (SvelteKit's `kit.version.name` default), not a git SHA. The only CI pipeline in the repo (`.github/workflows/roadmap.yml`) targets a DIFFERENT deployment (`docs.mvox.eu/roadmap` via GitHub Pages) and never touches mvox.eu's build. mvox.eu's actual build/deploy is CF Pages' own git-integration (build triggered directly by CF watching GitHub pushes), not a workflow in this repo, so this repo's Actions runs have no visibility into that build at all.
findings.evidence: `find src -iname '*version*'` finds no version-stamping source; `.svelte-kit/output/client/_app/version.json` = `{"version":"1788333181103"}` (a timestamp, not a SHA). perotin.md:692 records a live probe: 'No commit SHA is served in the HTML/JS (Path C SPA shell is the same for every route) ... `/_app/version.json` gives a build timestamp.' `.github/workflows/roadmap.yml` full content read — its only jobs fetch GH issues and deploy a rendered board to GitHub Pages; no reference to mvox.eu/CF Pages anywhere in it. [unverified] whether CF Pages' own build environment exposes `CF_PAGES_COMMIT_SHA` (a documented CF Pages built-in env var per Cloudflare's own docs) to the build step — plausible from general CF Pages knowledge but not confirmed against CF's docs or this project's CF dashboard in this session.

findings.topic: 3b/3c. Runtime fetch (GitHub raw/API) and other in-repo read-at-runtime patterns
findings.fact: No existing code in the repo fetches its own GitHub repo content at runtime (no octokit/raw.githubusercontent usage found outside the roadmap board's own issue-fetching script, which is a build-time GH Actions step, not a runtime app call). No general 'read a repo file at request time' pattern exists in the app.
findings.evidence: `scripts/roadmap/fetch-issues.ts` fetches GitHub *issues* via the GitHub API at CI build time (not runtime, not repo file content) — the only GitHub-API-calling code in the repo. No other match for GitHub raw-content fetch in src/ or scripts/.

findings.topic: 4. Non-app endpoints, routing, auth hooks
findings.fact: mvox.eu serves exactly one non-UI static file today: `robots.txt` (`User-agent: *` / `Allow: /`). There is no `hooks.server.ts` (none exists — confirmed empty find), so there is no global auth gate at all to interact with a new `/mcp` route; any auth that exists is client-side-only (guards checked in-component, e.g. `src/lib/auth/guard.ts`). No `_headers`/`_redirects` CF Pages routing files exist either. Because of `fallback: 'index.html'`, an unmatched path like `/mcp` today returns HTTP 200 with the SPA shell (not a 404), since there's no catch-all route or top-level `+error.svelte` — CF Pages' static-adapter fallback serves the same `index.html` for anything unrecognized.
findings.evidence: `static/`/`build/` directory listings show only `robots.txt` beside the SPA output. `find src -iname hooks*` empty. `find . -iname '_headers' -o -iname '_redirects'` empty (checked repo root and build/). `find src/routes -iname '*[...]*'` (catch-all route) and top-level `+error.svelte` both empty — confirms the fallback path is genuinely uncaught client-side.

findings.topic: 5. Doc size — payload feasibility
findings.fact: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md is 21,775 bytes / 190 lines. Trivially small for verbatim serving in any MCP response (well under any realistic Worker request/response-size or MCP payload ceiling).
findings.evidence: `wc -c` / `wc -l` on the file directly (docs/ is explicitly safe to read per task instructions, not gated behind origin/main).

findings.topic: 5b. #317 (stable identifiers) is not yet done — #318 is genuinely blocked
findings.fact: The doc currently has only positional section headers (§1 through §7.3, e.g. '## 3. Per-property sharing IS first-class...  [P]'), no non-positional stable IDs. #317 is open, labeled `in research`, not closed.
findings.evidence: `grep -n '^#'` on the doc lists only `## 1.` … `## 7.3` style headers, no ID scheme. `gh issue view 317` shows `state: OPEN`, labels `in research, ready, task`, unchecked acceptance boxes for the identifier scheme.

findings.topic: 6. #316's pre-flight-checklist question (report-only, not resolved)
findings.fact: The claim-lookup tools spec'd for #318 (`rights_rule(id)`, `rights_rules(topic)`) are stateless single-rule verbatim fetches keyed by an identifier or a topic string — no notion of a proposed change, no aggregation across rules, no pass/fail state. A pre-flight checklist tool is described in #318 itself as 'task-shaped' vs 'claim-shaped', and #316 explicitly notes neither of the two 2026-09-10 misreadings (both claim-shaped, mid-conversation) would have been caught by a checklist — implying the checklist targets a different failure mode (a schema change proposed without checking the relevant rule set at all, rather than a claim stated wrong). Building it would need, at minimum: (a) a way to take a structured description of a proposed schema change as input rather than a bare identifier/topic, (b) a rule-to-change-shape index (which rules apply to 'new entity type', 'flip _inheritrights', 'new _sharing value', etc.) beyond the flat identifier/topic lookup #318 already provides, (c) a checklist/gate output shape (per-item pass/fail/needs-answer) rather than a single verbatim rule return.
findings.evidence: #318 text ('Worth settling during research' section) and #316 text (COMMISSION note + 'Why a document alone is not the answer' section) both read directly via `gh issue view`. The (a)-(c) requirements are [speculative] — inferred from the claim-shaped-vs-task-shaped framing in the issues, not sourced from any design doc that spells out the checklist tool's shape.

r319.summary: Repo is read-only-clean (origin=mvox-dev/mvox-app.git). No .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ exists at all today (neither forms nor md, no config.yml) — only .github/workflows/roadmap.yml. The mvox side's citation-relevant law ([unverified]/[speculative]) lives ONLY in the user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, not in any of the 9 team role prompts (teams/mvox-dev/prompts/*.md) or in common-prompt.md — grep for 'unverified'/'speculative'/'cite' hits zero files there. The one place a claim-time citation rule DOES already exist is inside docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md itself (line 186), which is exactly the failure #316/#319 describe: the rule lives only inside the doc it governs. findings.topic: 1. .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE state

A much larger set of files use bare `§N` that resolve to THEIR OWN document's internal section numbers (design specs, migration handbooks, plans) rather than the rights doc — those are not orphaned by #317, only the six above are. Widest raw sweep (all `§[0-9]` hits, workspace-app + schema repo + auto-memory) returned ~340 lines across dozens of files; the schema repo (~/workspace) had zero `§` hits, and auto-memory had zero literal `§` hits (only bracket-topic memory files referencing rights mechanics by name, see finding 3).

findings.topic: 4a. Axis — multi-db (polyphony vs crede): does the rights doc distinguish per-db behavior
findings.fact: No — the doc states Entu rights/visibility mechanics as universal source-level facts (entu-api file:line reads), not scoped per database. The only per-db language is evidentiary (which db a probe was RUN on), never a claim that the mechanic differs by db: §7.3's supersession rule is corroborated on BOTH polyphony (synthetic, live-probed) AND crede's own real `/history` audit log showing the identical pattern — used as cross-db confirmation that the rule is one mechanic, not two.

No line asserts crede and polyphony behave differently under Entu's rights mechanics.

findings.topic: 4b. Axis — locales: is any of this user-facing, what language
findings.fact: Two separate, non-overlapping language surfaces exist and neither is threatened by file-path collision with the live pipeline. (i) The app's user-facing i18n is English/Estonian/Latvian/Ukrainian via Paraglide bundles under messages/*.json and src/*/paraglide/messages — untouched by #316's scope. (ii) GitHub issue bodies (including #317/#318/#319 themselves) carry an Estonian-language `slugline`+`lead` YAML front-matter convention (e.g. #317: "Iga õiguste reegel saab püsiva viitenumbri") that is NOT documented anywhere in teams/mvox-dev/*.md as a written rule — it only appears inside issue-body front matter and pipeline-args JSON, i.e. a Gama/PO-side authoring convention, not an app i18n concern. The rights rule text itself (what #318's MCP would serve verbatim) is English-only prose from the source doc; there is no Estonian/other-locale version and the epic's "verbatim" requirement (#318) implies there should not be one.

findings.topic: 4c. Axis — rights tiers: should the mcp endpoint be public or gated (decision point, not decided)
findings.fact: The rights doc's own evidence trail names a real person tied to a REAL pilot's rights data, not synthetic polyphony data: §7.3's corroborating case is "Joosep Loidap's standalone `_editor` on crede's database entity" vanishing when he was granted `_owner` — crede is documented elsewhere as a real-PII pilot (not the synthetic polyphony sandbox). If #318's MCP server serves this rule verbatim including its evidence/citation trail, an ungated/public endpoint would republish a real person's name in connection with a real rights-management investigation on a live collective's database. The epic (#316) says "both boards' agents reach it" (mvox-dev + po-team), which argues for broad-but-authenticated reach rather than fully public/anonymous — this is a decision point for whoever builds #318, not resolved here.
